items.hook: The SU(2) BFSS ground state, solved numerically, matches matrix bootstrap results to five figures.
items.summary: The authors solve for the ground-state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics and check it against bootstrap bounds and a known three-point amplitude. They also extract four-point scattering with Luscher's method, find the expected v^4/r^7 interaction, and report bound states and resonances. The gauge group is only SU(2), so the results may not carry over to large N.
items.title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model

items.hook: Randomized online graph coloring provably beats every deterministic algorithm.
items.summary: The paper tightens the competitive ratio for coloring graphs as their vertices arrive one at a time. It proves a deterministic lower bound of n/log n and a randomized upper bound near n(log log n)^2/log^2 n, which together separate the two kinds of algorithm. A gap of (log log n)^2 remains for randomized algorithms, and the randomized advantage holds against an oblivious adversary only.
items.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms

items.hook: Nonreal polynomial roots form a connected set only when the height is h = q(q-1).
items.summary: Collecting the nonreal roots of integer polynomials with coefficients up to height h, the closure is connected exactly at pronic heights 2, 6, 12, 20 and so on, and has at least five components otherwise. The proofs compare values and derivatives of power series near a real double zero. This settles a twenty-year-old numerical observation at height two. Whether non-pronic heights always give infinitely many components is shown only for many cases.
items.title: The closure of the nonreal roots of bounded-height polynomials is connected exactly at pronic heights

items.hook: A redesigned HaloTag reacts only with a modified substrate, allowing two targets to be labeled in cells.
items.summary: OrthoTag, made by structure-guided design and directed evolution, reacts with a modified chloroalkane and ignores HaloTag's substrate, and the reverse. Purified-protein rates show 109-fold mutual orthogonality, and two-color labeling worked in mammalian cells. Tests were limited to cultured cells and a small set of labeling experiments.
items.title: Design and Evolution of an Orthogonal HaloTag for Multiplexed Labeling in Cells
items.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

items.hook: In theory, gravitational phase evolution is distinguishable from classical mediators despite dephasing.
items.summary: In a dephased version of the Bose-Marletto-Vedral setup, the authors prove an exact finite-time difference between gravitational conditional-phase dynamics and any passive classical-mediator model, even when no entanglement forms. The difference survives some classical measurement and feedback. It is a theoretical result that depends on the chosen classical mediator models and on well-characterized local dephasing.
items.title: Testing non-classical gravitational phase dynamics under strong dephasing

items.hook: In a model, line cooling sets where an AGN's warm corona ends, at a sharp iron ionization front.

readout.label: Internal heating at the corona transition

items.summary: Spectral modeling of a warm corona above an accretion disk shows its outer edge is set where line cooling replaces Compton cooling, at an iron ionization front. A larger corona gives a bigger soft X-ray excess, matching recent changing-look AGN findings. The result comes from a simulated model with fixed assumptions, not from fitting a specific source.
items.title: The Edge of the Warm Corona in Active Galactic Nuclei

items.hook: The brown dwarf desert is set by mass ratio, not mass: companions drop sharply near q of 2%.
items.summary: Joint modeling of Hipparcos and Gaia astrometry for 63,254 stars shows companions are depleted at a mass ratio near 2% from M to B stars, which rules out a desert at fixed companion mass. Occurrence also trends differently with metallicity below and above the desert, hinting at two formation channels. The data cover only 3 to 94 year orbits, about 2 to 20 au.
items.title: The Brown Dwarf Desert is a Mass-Ratio Desert: Astrometric Demographics of 63,254 Stars

items.hook: Ashbaugh's 1999 conjecture is false: the ball does not maximize the buckling eigenvalue ratio.
items.hook_turn: the ball does not maximize the buckling eigenvalue ratio.
items.summary: The authors build smooth domains with a few interior holes whose ratio of the first two clamped buckling eigenvalues beats the ball's, in every dimension of 2 or more. A thin zero-value sphere near a ball's boundary raises both eigenvalues equally at first order, but their ratio rises at second order. The counterexamples are perforated domains, so the ratio for simply connected shapes is not settled by this.
items.title: Counterexamples to the buckling eigenvalue-ratio conjecture in every dimension

items.hook: Every 2-coloring of the plane has a monochromatic copy of any triangle with side ratio sqrt(7/3).
items.summary: The paper confirms the Erdos et al. conjecture for triangles with a ratio of sqrt(7/3) between two sides, and shows that any coloring of the plane has monochromatic or rainbow copies of 36 specific triangles. Both results come from analyzing finite configurations on the triangular lattice. The general conjecture for all non-equilateral triangles remains open.
items.title: Monochromatic or rainbow triangles in the triangular lattice

items.hook: The ten martini problem is solved for the positive-Lyapunov spectrum of analytic Schrodinger operators.
items.summary: The authors settle the ten martini problem, a question about the Cantor structure of the spectrum, for the positive-Lyapunov part of any nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schrodinger operator. They extend an almost-reducibility strategy from two-dimensional to arbitrary finite-dimensional centers using a symplectic structure. The result covers the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum only.
items.title: The Supercritical Ten Martini Problem

items.hook: Telescope mirrors can turn solar dark photons into X-rays, and BabyIAXO could catch them.
items.summary: Longitudinal solar dark photons, the dominant type below about 1 eV, were missed by past searches. Using Maxwell's equations at a boundary, the author shows they produce light when they hit a grazing-incidence mirror. BabyIAXO would match the XENON1T limits and IAXO would go deeper, but only if sensitivity reaches 10 eV; this is a forecast, not a measurement.
items.title: Long(itudinal) live the helioscope: novel bounds on solar dark photons from conversion on reflecting surfaces

items.hook: In a superconductor, a hidden spin supercurrent can cancel a resistive spin current, theory shows.
items.summary: Spin currents usually fade by losing angular momentum to relaxation. The authors show that a superconductor with a spin-splitting field can instead carry an opposing condensate spin current, so total spin and charge currents vanish. This is a theoretical result, and the proposed spin-to-charge signals have not been measured.
items.title: Hidden Spin-Supercurrent Counterflow in Conventional Superconductors

items.hook: First SPHEREx search for axion dark matter finds no signal and sets new limits on light coupling.
items.hook_turn: sets new limits on light coupling.
items.summary: Axion-like dark matter would decay into faint infrared light, so the team searched the first 16.5 months of SPHEREx spectra for it. They found no signal and set limits for masses of 0.496 to 3.32 eV that rival earlier ones. The analysis is deliberately conservative, and the authors say better methods could improve it by over ten times.
items.title: First constraints on axion-like particles with SPHEREx data

items.hook: In a simulated moire model, doping three different phases always yields the same chiral superconductor.
items.summary: The authors studied a Hubbard model on a lattice with magnetic flux, which may be realizable in twisted bilayers. DMRG and quantum Monte Carlo simulations find a quantum Hall phase, a chiral spin liquid, and an antiferromagnet, and doping each gives the same chiral superconductor. These are numerical results on a model; no experiment has shown this.
items.title: Chiral Superconductivity Indifferent to Parent Topology in the Square-Lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard Model

items.hook: Lithium was measured in 209 giant stars of the Small Magellanic Cloud, including 4 lithium-rich ones.

readout.label: Red giant stars with lithium measured in the SMC

items.summary: Lithium in other galaxies is hard to measure because only bright giants near the tip of the red giant branch can be observed. VLT spectra of 209 such stars show large star-to-star scatter, which models attribute to mixing in the stars and to nova enrichment at lower metallicity. Only about a third have firm lithium detections, and the rest give upper limits.
items.title: The chemical DNA of the Magellanic Clouds -- VII. The lithium abundance in the Small Magellanic Cloud and the discovery of 4 lithium-rich stars

items.hook: Normal approximation over convex sets has a sharp fourth-moment threshold for dimension scaling.
items.summary: The paper proves explicit Berry-Esseen bounds on how well sums of independent random vectors match a Gaussian over any convex set. For i.i.d. sums it finds the optimal dependence on sample size, dimension and moments, with matching lower bounds. Fourth moments are the first order that gives an error linear in dimension. The result concerns worst-case bounds, so typical cases may do better.
items.title: Sharp and explicit Berry--Esseen inequalities over convex sets

items.hook: Checking each LLM math step with algebra software as it is written cut wrong answers by up to 14.9%.
items.hook_turn: cut wrong answers by up to 14.9%.
items.summary: Instead of using a second model to check reasoning, the method sends each symbolic math step to a computer algebra system and tells the model when a step fails. On the ASyMoB benchmark with three open-weights models, accuracy rose 1.4 to 5.6 points for 6-7% more tokens. It only works where steps can be checked by code, here symbolic math.
items.title: Catch It Where It Happens: Real Time Error Correction During LLM Reasoning

items.hook: A quantum photon counter can see finite irreversibility while the true entropy production is infinite.
items.summary: The author builds a model of a parametric oscillator coupled to a vacuum bath, where forward and reverse processes cannot overlap, so microscopic entropy production diverges. A realistic photon counter with imperfect efficiency and dark counts still reports a finite, positive arrow of time. This is a proof on a constructed model, not an experiment.
items.title: Finite Measured Entropy Production Does Not Imply Finite Microscopic Irreversibility

items.hook: FusionQ decodes quantum errors in local pieces and matches the exact global answer on every shot.
items.summary: Quantum error decoders usually wait for a full block of syndrome data. FusionQ decodes small regions around triggered detectors as data arrives and fuses them, with a proof that an exact local solver gives the global most likely error. It cuts latency across decoder types, though the evaluation appears to be in simulation rather than on hardware.
items.title: FusionQ: A Generic and Optimal Decoding Framework for Ultra-Low-Latency Quantum Error Correction

items.hook: At least 22% of white dwarfs with hydrogen in helium atmospheres got it from planetary material.

readout.label: Min. share with accreted hydrogen, DB white dwarfs

items.summary: Some white dwarfs with helium atmospheres show hydrogen, and its origin has been debated. A simple model with both internal and accreted sources was tested against DESI and SDSS samples of DB white dwarfs, requiring at least 22 +/- 2 percent to have accreted it from ices or hydrated minerals. The result depends on the model and applies to a limited temperature range.
items.title: Planetary material is a major source of hydrogen in helium-atmosphere white dwarfs

items.hook: Summing over all subspaces of a vector space takes N log N time, like the classic subset transform.
items.summary: Summing values over all subspaces of a finite-field vector space was thought to need slower lattice methods. The authors give a time algorithm proportional to N log N for N subspaces, with uses in Grassmann graph computations and graph coloring. Tests show speedups of up to 18 times on some tasks, with Lean 4 proofs of the identities. The gains are for these structured problems only.
items.title: A Fast Algorithm for Subspace Convolution

items.hook: Debris transiting a white dwarf switches between 9.94 and 11.17 hour periods within weeks.
items.summary: Hubble ultraviolet spectra of ZTF J0328-1219 fit accretion of a chondritic body, and 16 days of 2025 photometry show the dominant transit period changing from 9.937 to 11.17 hours and back. The changes suggest collisions in the debris. It is one system over a short campaign, and a possible 7.64 hour period is uncertain.
items.title: Near-Ultraviolet and Optical Observations of the White Dwarf ZTF J0328$-$1219 Reveal Variable Periodicity in its Transiting Debris System

items.hook: The modular curve X_1(42) needs degree 12 before it gets infinitely many rational points.

readout.label: Q-gonality of the modular curve X_1(42)

items.summary: The Q-gonality of X_1(42) is 12, up from a proven lower bound of 10, so 12 is the lowest degree with infinitely many points. The proof is a computer search of 743,231 Riemann-Roch spaces, cut down using a cyclic group of symmetries of order 12. An older, slower search gave the same answer. The result covers this one curve and rests on exhaustive computation.
items.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$

items.hook: Microbes meet sinking marine snow most at 14.4 m/day, and far less once it sinks faster than 78.1 m/day.

readout.label: Sinking speed at peak microbial encounter rate

items.summary: Microbes at sea swim toward sinking marine snow only within a limited zone, and fast sinking shrinks that zone. The team tracked single cells around freshly collected aggregates on a ship under imposed flows, then fed the measured encounter rates into a transport model. Encounter rates peak at 14.4 m/day. The measurements come from limited shipboard samples, so the model's reach to the whole ocean is untested.
items.title: Chemotactic Horizons Regulate Threshold Dynamics in the Biological Carbon Pump

items.hook: One small black hole merger can wipe out 2 to 3 orders of magnitude of a dark matter spike.
items.summary: Dark matter spikes around massive black holes could be spotted through gravitational-wave dephasing, but mergers destroy them. Simulations of binary inspirals show even a 0.005 mass-ratio merger cuts central density sharply. Combined with merger histories from the Horizon-AGN simulation, this limits detectable spikes to black holes of 10^6 to 5x10^7 solar masses. The results are simulation-based and assume spikes form in the first place.
items.title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers

items.hook: Baumslag-Solitar groups act C^1 on an interval only when |m| equals |n|.
items.summary: The authors settle exactly when the group BS(m,n) can be realized by once-differentiable orientation-preserving maps of the interval: only when |n| = |m|. For slightly smoother maps (C^(1+alpha)) the list shrinks to a few trivial cases. This is a pure proof, and it covers integers m and n other than -1, 0 and 1.
items.title: Smooth actions of Baumslag-Solitar groups on the interval

items.hook: A partial view of a quantum code leaks exactly 1 minus 2 times the failure rate of decoding on that view.
items.summary: For any region of a toric code and any Pauli noise, an eavesdropper's best advantage in learning a logical bit equals 1 - 2 P_fail, where P_fail is the failure rate of decoding using only that region. A region missing one column of the code learns nothing, and a strip's threshold matches the Nishimori point of the random-bond Ising model. Tests on two IBM Heron processors (d = 3, 5) use an emulated adversary, not a real attack.
items.title: How wide must an eavesdropper be? Leakage of a toric-code logical bit to a strip and the Nishimori point

items.hook: An X-point target divertor cut peak outer heat flux by 40 to 60% in high-power tokamak tests.
items.summary: A tokamak exhaust design called the X-point target was compared with a conventional single-null divertor at 2.5 MW on the TCV tokamak. It lowered peak outer target heat flux and allowed detachment with nitrogen seeding where the conventional design could not. Reversing the magnetic field showed that E x B drifts cause uneven detachment across strike points. The tests were in L-mode on one machine, which is smaller than a reactor.
items.title: High-power X-Point Target divertor experiments on the TCV tokamak

items.hook: Dust lag around small black holes grows with luminosity at a slope of 0.47, just under the 0.5 expected.
items.summary: Dust around growing black holes echoes their optical flicker in infrared light, and the delay gives the dust distance. Using ZTF and WISE data for 65 low-mass active galactic nuclei, the authors extend the radius-luminosity relation over nearly seven orders of magnitude. The slightly shallow slope may reflect shadowing by slim disks or imperfect luminosity proxies. Both explanations are suggested, not tested directly.
items.title: Dust Reverberation Mapping of Low-Mass Active Galactic Nuclei

items.hook: Eccentric black hole mergers may reveal line-of-sight acceleration over ten times better than circular ones.
items.summary: Binaries with eccentric orbits could show whether a nearby object accelerates them, through a small shift in the gravitational-wave phase. Analyzing the signal from the first eccentric harmonic, not the usual one, adds a longer stretch of signal. Fisher forecasts and full Bayesian runs show constraints improve by more than ten times at e_20 near 0.1 for strong signals, and about 5 times for weak ones. These are simulated signals and need fast eccentric waveform models.
items.title: Eccentricity greatly enhances the detectability of line-of-sight acceleration in gravitational wave signals

items.hook: Reversing a knot's direction can change its complexity in Thompson's group, as the knot 8_17 shows.
items.summary: Thompson's groups can build every link, and the Thompson index counts how complex a knot is within them. The author proves bounds from the Jones and HOMFLY-PT polynomials and computes the indices for prime knots up to 13 crossings by exhaustive search with certified results. Hundreds of non-invertible knots differ from their reverses, and one index separates the Conway knot from its mutant. Some indices are only fully determined up to 8 to 12 crossings.
items.title: Thompson indices of knots and the invertibility problem

items.hook: The smallest hole-free mirrored lattice room with an unlit point has 12 sides.

readout.label: Fewest sides, hole-free room with one source

items.summary: Rooms with mirrored walls can hold points that no light ray connects. The authors classify the smallest such rooms built from tilings, finding the 12-sided pinwheel for one source on the isosceles right triangle tiling and 16 sides on the square tiling. They count all smallest rooms for two sources, such as 12 rooms with 24 sides. Many results use exhaustive computer searches within bounds proved by hand, and they cover tiling-based rooms only.
items.title: Unilluminable rooms: minimal examples, classifications and exceptions

items.hook: A robot arm ran chemistry kit experiments from a photo of the printed sheet, completing 9 of 10 runs.
items.summary: Curie's Jarvis lets a Franka Panda arm work on an ordinary bench: it reads steps from a photo, finds containers without markers, and reads their labels. It finished 5 of 5 runs of one children's kit protocol and 4 of 5 of another with no human help. In 160 label locates, it identified every container. Only two simple protocols were tested, so harder chemistry is unproven.
items.title: Curie's Jarvis: Autonomous Robotic Chemistry Experiments from Printed Protocols

items.hook: A new starlight model makes JWST planet imaging 2 to 15 times more sensitive.
items.summary: Imaging a planet means removing the star's glare, which standard methods do with reference images that drift out of date. This method fits a physical model of the instrument with millions of parameters using automatic differentiation. On JWST NIRCam coronagraph data it beat standard techniques by 2 to 15 times and detected 51 Eridani b at 4.3 microns for the first time. It was shown on JWST observations only, not yet other telescopes.
items.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit

items.hook: Swirling fluid in a cylinder with total slip stays smooth forever if its initial swirl is small enough.
items.summary: The paper proves that axisymmetric Navier-Stokes solutions in a finite cylinder with zero-friction slip stay smooth for all time. This holds when the initial swirl has zero mean and a scale-invariant smallness condition holds. The proof uses a trace identity and an L^4 bound that replaces the lost maximum principle. The smallness condition limits the result, and the general large-data question stays open.
items.title: Global regularity of axisymmetric Navier--Stokes equations under total slip and critical smallness

items.hook: A bright high-energy interlayer exciton near 2.23 eV appears in few-layer WSe2
items.summary: Researchers found a narrow, bright high-energy interlayer exciton in few-layer WSe2 whose emission grows with thickness. Calculations point to mixing of intralayer and interlayer states as the cause. In a sliding-ferroelectric stack, its energy shifts with polarization, so moving domain walls can be tracked optically. The explanation of the brightening rests on calculations, and the device study covers one stack type.
items.title: Hybridization-brightened interlayer excitons in multilayer WSe2 controlled by sliding ferroelectricity

items.hook: Spinning dust clouds obey the hoop conjecture within 14% if rotational energy counts toward mass
items.hook_turn: if rotational energy counts toward mass

readout.label: Max hoop coefficient deviation from unity

items.summary: The hoop conjecture says a black hole forms when enough mass fits inside a small enough hoop in every direction. The authors built initial data for rotating dust shaped like pancakes and baguettes and tested it numerically. It holds when the mass includes rotational energy, but using the ADM mass gives apparent violations up to about 25%. The test covers axisymmetric dust only.
items.title: Challenging the hoop conjecture with spinning pancakes and baguettes

items.hook: A weight exists where an entire function looks small yet stays a positive distance from all polynomials
items.summary: This paper answers a question of Borichev in the negative. The authors construct a growing weight and an entire function of zero exponential type that is small relative to the weight, yet cannot be approximated by polynomials in the weighted norms. The result is a specific counterexample and says nothing about how common such weights are.
items.title: A Counterexample to Polynomial Approximation for Monotone Weights

items.hook: Simulations show freezing impact melt could push enough water up to build Ceres's pingo-like mounds
items.summary: Occator Crater on Ceres has mounds that resemble Earth's pingos. Heat transfer and groundwater flow simulations of a freezing impact melt deposit show pressure gradients strong enough to drive fluid to the surface through hydraulic fracturing. Delivered water volumes meet or exceed what pingo formation needs across most tested parameters. This is modeling only, and the regolith properties are assumed.
items.title: Cryohydrologic Flow and Pingo Formation Within Freezing Impact Melts in Occator Crater, Ceres

items.hook: Every hyperbolic knot has a braid diagram where each crossing is faithfully tracked, settling a conjecture
items.summary: The paper proves that any hyperbolic knot has a closed braid diagram with distinct parabolic fixed points at every crossing, answering a conjecture of McPhail-Snyder. The proof rewrites a troublesome crossing as five ordinary ones, using at most 2n-1 letters per replaced crossing on n strands. It is a pure existence result and does not address how to find the shortest such diagram.
items.title: Every hyperbolic knot has an arc-faithful closed braid diagram
